newsitem.title: UK: UK casino industry welcomes deregulation proposals.
newsitem.headline: UK casino industry welcomes deregulation proposals.

text.p: The British Casino Association (BCA) on Tuesday welcomed the latest government proposals to deregulate their industry.

"For too long the British public has been kept in the dark about the casino industry. Our members have not even been allowed an entry in Yellow Pages," BCA General Secretary Brian Lemon said in a statement.

"The casino industry has been stuck in a timewarp of 1960s regulation but operating in the 1990s world of fierce competition," added Lemon, whose association represents Britain's 118 licensed casinos.

"These proposals recognise that the world has moved on. We do not want wholesale deregulation but these proposals will allow us to offer better facilities to our home players and attract overseas visitors."

Under the proposals, casinos will be permitted in a further seven towns while restrictions on advertising will be eased and membership made easier. It will be possible to introduce more slot machines and the 250 stg slot machine jackpot lifted.
The proposals, contained in a government consultation document, would allow casinos to advertise in non-national newspapers and magazines for the first time.

The government lists seven "conference" towns where casinos will be allowed to open. This is in addition to 13 towns in the London area and the provinces named in an initial consultation document issued in February.
